title: Does systematic coronary imaging with guideline-directed prevention improve outcomes after type 2 myocardial infarction?

pico.population: Adults with adjudicated type 2 MI (Fourth Universal Definition)
pico.intervention: Systematic coronary CTA (with invasive angiography for significant disease) plus protocolised secondary prevention
pico.comparator: Usual care without systematic coronary evaluation
pico.outcomes: Cardiovascular death, MI, HF hospitalisation and all-cause death
pico.timing: Randomisation during index admission; follow-up at least 2 years

decision: Whether to image the coronary arteries and start long-term prevention after type 2 MI rather than treat only the precipitant
why_now: Observational studies report high MACE after type 2 MI and a high prevalence of previously unrecognised coronary disease, yet no randomised evidence exists.

designs.primary: Registry-based randomised trial embedded in a national MI or hospital-episode registry
designs.alternative: Target trial emulation of coronary CTA or angiography within 30 days versus none in linked national data

data_required: Adjudicated type 2 MI cases with linked outcomes
data_sources: Linked national registers (for example MINAP-type audits with HES), SWEDEHEART-style registry platforms, UK Biobank extract for emulation
feasibility: Trial needs a registry partner and consortium; the emulation is deliverable with current access but suffers confounding by indication.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects. Complements owner registry-embedded trial methodology.

G1.note: Common decision; hard outcomes (death, MI, HF hospitalisation) in a population with 1-year mortality of 13.8% in PMID 29020401.

G2.note: No randomised trial of any strategy in type 2 MI in the input files; Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No ongoing type 2 MI trial in the trials file; the IPD meta-analysis PMID 41553312 (2026-05-05) is prognostic and does not address treatment.

G4.note: A pragmatic registry-based randomised comparison would be citable by a guideline committee; observational emulation alone would not resolve confounding by indication.

G5.note: Not a repeat synthesis; first randomised treatment-strategy question in type 2 MI.

impact.why: Type 2 MI is a large fraction of troponin-positive admissions (22% rise in diagnosis in PMID 31587565) with mortality comparable to type 1 MI.

novelty.why: No randomised treatment evidence appears in the inputs.

equipoise.why: Practice varies and the aetiology-directed benefit of coronary evaluation is untested.

design.why: Heterogeneous precipitants and imaging uptake complicate a pragmatic trial.

timeliness.why: A 2026 IPD meta-analysis (PMID 41553312) has just defined the risk.

citation.why: Large pragmatic trials in untreated populations are suited to the target journals.

feasibility.why: Requires a registry consortium and funding; emulation is feasible in the short term.

next_actions: Extract coronary imaging yield and outcome estimates from PMID 35341327 and PMID 37777947 for sample size inputs
Approach a registry partner about embedding randomisation
Draft a target trial specification as a fallback emulation

title: Is initiation of statin, renin-angiotensin or beta-blocker therapy after type 2 MI associated with lower cardiovascular events in national linked data?

pico.population: Adults discharged after type 2 MI without prior use of the drug class
pico.intervention: Initiation of statin, ACE inhibitor or ARB, or beta-blocker within 30 days of discharge
pico.outcomes: Cardiovascular death, MI, HF hospitalisation, all-cause death
pico.timing: Time zero at discharge; follow-up up to 5 years

decision: Whether to prescribe long-term preventive therapy after type 2 MI
why_now: Type 2 MI has an adverse prognosis (PMID 41553312, PMID 31902228) but no trial of preventive drugs, and uptake in practice is unknown.

designs.primary: Target trial emulation in linked national registers or biobank
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial of a statin-based package

data_required: Type 2 MI diagnoses with prescribing and outcome linkage
data_sources: UK Biobank QMUL extract with hospital and primary care linkage; national audits; Scandinavian registers
feasibility: Owner has UK Biobank access; type 2 MI numbers in the biobank may be small and case ascertainment needs checking.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects. Uses owner UK Biobank experience.
target_journal: JAMA Cardiology or European Heart Journal

G1.note: Common prescribing decision with hard outcomes.

G2.note: No randomised evidence appears in the inputs; Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No ongoing trial of preventive drugs in type 2 MI in the trials file.

G4.note: Emulation can only partly address confounding by indication and uncertain diagnostic coding of type 2 MI; acceptable as hypothesis-generating unless a stated identification strategy and negative controls are shown.

G5.note: Not a repeat synthesis or a surrogate-only study.

impact.why: Large untreated population with high mortality.

novelty.why: No drug-class evidence after type 2 MI appears in the inputs.

equipoise.why: Treatment effect unknown; no randomised data.

design.why: Confounding by indication and coding validity limit credibility.

timeliness.why: Fits the recent prognostic IPD synthesis.

citation.why: Observational emulation in a niche population is likely to suit a cardiology main journal only if well identified.

feasibility.why: Owner has UK Biobank and emulation methods.

next_actions: Count type 2 MI cases and drug initiation in UK Biobank
Write a target trial protocol with negative control outcomes
Validate case definitions against adjudicated cohorts such as PMID 32138959

title: Does routine postoperative troponin surveillance with a protocolised response reduce cardiovascular events after major noncardiac surgery?

pico.population: Adults aged 45 years or older having major noncardiac surgery
pico.intervention: Routine postoperative hs-troponin surveillance with a protocolised cardiology response to myocardial injury
pico.outcomes: Major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause death at 1 year
pico.timing: Postoperative days 1 to 3 for testing; follow-up 1 year

decision: Whether hospitals should adopt systematic postoperative troponin surveillance
decision_maker: Perioperative physicians, anaesthetists, surgeons and cardiologists
why_now: Cohort data show high mortality associated with perioperative injury (PMID 28444280, PMID 29203498, PMID 36705050), and MANAGE (PMID 29900874) suggested a treatable target, but surveillance has not been tested.

competing.note: MINS, AKI and pulmonary pathology in acute abdominal surgery; allocation not applicable; not an adequately powered randomised test of surveillance.

designs.primary: Stepped-wedge cluster registry-based trial using hospital episode and audit data
designs.alternative: Target trial emulation using differential hospital surveillance policy as an instrument

data_required: Surgical episodes with postoperative troponin results and outcomes
data_sources: National surgical audit linked to HES; VISION-type cohort investigators
feasibility: Needs hospital engagement and a funded response protocol; population is very large.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects.
target_journal: Circulation, JAMA Cardiology or European Heart Journal

G2.note: Prognostic data exist but no trial tests surveillance; Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No adequately powered randomised surveillance trial in the trials file; NCT04681508 is small and non-randomised.

G4.note: Stepped-wedge registry design is a credible route; a cohort cannot separate detection from effect.

G5.note: Strategy question, not a repeat synthesis; endpoint is MACE, not troponin level.

impact.why: Millions of major surgeries; MINS is common (PMID 29203498 reports 16% of surgeries).

novelty.why: Surveillance has not been tested; treatment trials dominate the literature.

equipoise.why: Treatment effect of MINS therapy is uncertain (PMID 29900874 single positive trial; neutral trials in PMID 37640035, PMID 40884771, PMID 40511609).

design.why: Needs an effective response protocol or the trial tests only detection.

timeliness.why: Several MINS prevention trials are due to report.

citation.why: Perioperative strategy trials of this size reach the general and target tiers.

next_actions: Define the response protocol from MANAGE (PMID 29900874) and the AHA statement (PMID 34601955)
Identify national audit data with postoperative troponin

title: Do rapid rule-out pathways for suspected MI differ in 12-month ischaemic events: a reconstructed-IPD synthesis of randomised pathway trials timed to DanRUSH?

pico.population: Patients with suspected MI in the emergency department
pico.intervention: Accelerated hs-troponin rule-out (0/1h, single low threshold, point-of-care or prehospital)
pico.outcomes: Death or MI at 30 days and 12 months; invasive angiography
pico.timing: Pre-specified update at the DanRUSH readout

decision: Which rule-out pathway to adopt and how long safety must be observed
why_now: 30-day non-inferiority (PMID 31478763) conflicts with a 12-month signal (PMID 33998255) and a non-inferiority failure (PMID 33752439).

competing.note: DanRUSH; rapid or ultra-rapid MI diagnosis.

designs.primary: Reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis of randomised rule-out pathway trials with registered protocol and pre-specified update

data_required: Published Kaplan-Meier curves and event counts from randomised pathway trials
feasibility: Fully deliverable with the owner's reconstructed-IPD workflow.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects. Matches the same-day SRMA workflow.

G1.note: Very common decision, with safety defined by death and MI.

G2.note: Trials conflict on safety at different horizons; Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: DanRUSH (NCT07727135, N 28000, 2028-09-01) is an adequately powered randomised trial expected within 24 months of 24 October 2026; only the timed update angle survives.

G4.note: Pre-registered pooled analysis with the readout update is citable.

G5.note: Reconstructed IPD addresses horizon-specific effects, not a repeat of pooled estimates, though the trial set is small.

impact.why: Rule-out decisions are made on millions of presentations.

novelty.why: Individual trials are published; horizon-specific pooling is new.

equipoise.why: Safety signal at 12 months in one trial against non-inferiority at 30 days.

citation.why: Diagnostic pathway syntheses are cited but rarely top decile.

next_actions: Register the protocol on PROSPERO with a pre-specified DanRUSH update
Extract Kaplan-Meier curves from PMID 33998255 and PMID 31478763

title: Does colchicine reduce myocardial injury and cardiovascular events after noncardiac surgery: synthesis timed to the POPCORN and COLCAT readouts?

pico.outcomes: Myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery; MACE and death at 30 days
pico.timing: Update at readouts of NCT05618353 and NCT06279000

why_now: COP-AF did not show a significant MINS reduction (PMID 37640035) and further colchicine trials are due.
feasibility: Deliverable by the owner; trials are small.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects.

G1.note: Perioperative MI and death are hard outcomes.

G2.note: One neutral trial and several ongoing; Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No adequately powered trial is expected; the individual trials are small.

G4.note: A prospective synthesis is citable only if trials report hard outcomes.

G5.note: Pooling a few small trials with a biomarker-defined primary outcome is incremental and may not reach a parent journal.

impact.why: Large surgical population but uncertain effect size.

equipoise.why: One neutral trial and no confirmation.

citation.why: Small-trial pooled analyses seldom reach the top decile.
